context: Use the left-leaning 2-3 red-black tree variant (LLRB) for tree_type red_black, not CLRS-style red-black. Start from an empty tree (initial null) and apply the operations exactly in the given order; never sort or deduplicate. Insertion creates a red leaf and repairs on the way back up: left-rotate a right red link, right-rotate consecutive left red links, and flip colors to split temporary 4-nodes. Deletion moves red links toward the deletion path before descending, then restores left-leaning form on ascent; the root is normalized to black after every operation. The in-order successor (smallest key in the right subtree) replaces a deleted node with two children. Heights: empty subtree 0, leaf 1; balance is left height minus right height. Snapshots list nodes sorted by key. Recolors record only actual color changes in execution order, including root normalization and temporary flips; creating a fresh red leaf is not a recolor. Rotations and recolors are separate ordered traces. The user's request was: 'Start with an empty red-black tree. Insert 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, then delete 50. Show every intermediate tree, rotation, and color change.'
